claims.location: Theorem 1, PDF p1; proof pp2–3; TeX lines65–73,107–164
claims.claim: For each fixed SPD real inner product G on C²≅R⁴, the closed stable monic quadratic set is not prox-regular at (a,b)=(0,0). Every neighborhood contains an unstable input with at least two distinct attained global nearest points in that set.
claims.quantifiers: For every fixed G and every neighborhood, there exists an input and distinct minimizing stable polynomials. This is not a claim that every nearby unstable input has multiple projections.
claims.assumptions: p(z)=z²+az+b, complex a,b; α≤0; global coefficient distance.
claims.validation_status: Statement and cited theorem hypotheses mapped only; independent mathematical gates pending.

claims.location: Theorem 1, PDF p1; Section3, PDF p3; TeX185–215
claims.claim: The corresponding non-prox-regularity and arbitrarily nearby attained global projection ties hold in exact degree two, with varying nonzero leading coefficient near (ℓ,a,b)=(1,0,0), for every fixed SPD real metric on R⁶.
claims.assumptions: ℓ≠0; no reduction to a nonlinear coefficient pullback metric. Global attainment relies on the compact-ball localization written in Section3.

claims.claim: The whole abscissa epigraph fails set prox-regularity at height zero over the monic and full base points, for every fixed SPD real coefficient/height metric.
claims.assumptions: Epigraph height real. The limiting support covector is horizontal; its metric representative can tilt in mixed metrics.

claims.claim: The monic complex quadratic abscissa is function prox-regular at the origin relative to each finite limiting subgradient in the real Euclidean coefficient metric.
claims.assumptions: A fixed finite subgradient is specified first; neighborhood and curvature may depend on it. No all-subgradient uniformity or full-degree/function-metric theorem is asserted.
claims.validation_status: Definition/epigraph/composition primary references checked for scope; proof verification pending.

boundary_cases: Imaginary-axis and multiple roots are included (closed stability).
Real monic quadratics form the convex orthant a≥0,b≥0; the complex witness uses Im b≠0.
Exact degree excludes ℓ=0; full stable set is not globally closed.
Positive-definite means fixed SPD real matrix; singular/indefinite, moving metrics, arbitrary norms and arbitrary nonlinear parameter maps are outside the statement.
Global minimizers are asserted existentially; no explicit unstable target plus two minimizing polynomials is supplied.
Whole-set epigraph failure and finite-subgradient function prox-regularity are different conditions.
